title: Choosing a Private Service Edge design and node count

prose.text: Sizing is an arithmetic exercise with one assumption and two hard rules.

prose.label: Worked answers.
prose.text: {{worked-examples}} {{always-quoted-n-plus-one}} {{pse5-above-1gbps}} Whether the PSE 3 limit and the PSE 5 recommendation above 1 Gbps of download reconcile is open {{gap:pse3-above-1gbps-tension}}.

prose.label: The hard rule.
prose.text: {{over-5gbps-needs-dedicated-and-review}} {{above-5gbps-dedicated-budget}} The address and port budget per design is in [[zia.private-service-edge.ip-requirements]].

Design behavior (why a minimum of two nodes, how the LB pair works) is in [[zia.private-service-edge.cluster-architecture]]. Whether to deploy a PSE at all is [[zia.private-service-edge.when-to-deploy]].

checks.do: Size on total throughput in both directions, not download alone, using the assumed upload where upload is unknown.
Read the 'up to 24 Gbps' figure as upload across the LB instances, not as a total-throughput ceiling.

design-pse3.statement: Private Service Edge 3 with Integrated LB: 3 Service Edge instances, an integrated LB and a 1GE network interface, sized for ISP link speeds of 1 Gbps download.

quotes: | Private Service Edge 3 with Integrated LB | An annual subscription to Private Service Edge with 3 Service Edge instances, an integrated LB, and a 1GE network interface. | 1 Gbps |

design-pse5.statement: Private Service Edge 5 with Integrated LB: 5 Service Edge instances, an integrated LB and a 10GE network interface, sized for ISP link speeds of 2 Gbps download.

quotes: | Private Service Edge 5 with Integrated LB | An annual subscription to Private Service Edge with 5 Service Edge instances, an integrated LB, and a 10GE network interface. | 2 Gbps |

design-pse5-dedicated.statement: Private Service Edge 5 with Dedicated LB: 6 Service Edge instances, a dedicated LB with up to 4 LB instances and a 10GE network interface, sized for ISP link speeds greater than 5 Gbps download.

quotes: | Private Service Edge 5 with Dedicated LB | An annual subscription to Private Service Edge with 6 Service Edge instances, a dedicated LB with up to 4 LB instances, and a 10GE network interface. | Greater than 5 Gbps |

upload-assumption.statement: The sizing figures assume upload throughput is around 30% of download. When upload is unknown, 30% of the expected download is used.

quotes: The preceding sizing suggestion is based on the assumption that the upload throughput is around 30% of the download throughput.
If the upload throughput is unknown, 30% of the expected download throughput is considered as upload throughput based on the industry average.

size-both-directions.statement: Private Service Edge sizing is based on throughput, and both upload and download throughput must be considered.

quotes: You must consider both upload and download throughput when sizing a Private Service Edge deployment.

upload-caps.statement: Maximum upload throughput per cluster is limited to 800 Mbps on Private Service Edge 3, 2.5 Gbps on Private Service Edge 5, and 6 Gbps per LB instance on Private Service Edge 5 with Dedicated LB (up to 24 Gbps).

quotes: The maximum upload throughput per cluster is limited to 800 Mbps on Private Service Edge 3, 2.5 Gbps on Private Service Edge 5, and 6 Gbps per LB instance on Private Service Edge 5 with Dedicated LB.
| Maximum Upload Throughput per Cluster | 800 Mbps | 2.5 Gbps | Up to 24 Gbps |

cluster-totals.statement: A Private Service Edge 3 cluster handles up to 1.2 Gbps of download and 2 Gbps of total throughput; a Private Service Edge 5 cluster handles up to 3.9 Gbps of download and 5 Gbps of total throughput.

quotes: Private Service Edge 3 cluster handles up to 1.2 Gbps of download throughput and 2 Gbps of total throughput.
Private Service Edge 5 cluster services up to a maximum of 3.9 Gbps of download throughput and 5 Gbps of total throughput.

node-counts.statement: Maximum Private Service Edges per cluster is 3 for Private Service Edge 3 and 5 with Integrated LB and 10 for Private Service Edge 5 with Dedicated LB; the minimum is 2 for all three. The Dedicated LB design has 2 dedicated LBs per cluster.

quotes: | Maximum Private Service Edge per Cluster | 3 | 3 | 10 |
| Minimum Private Service Edge per Cluster | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| Dedicated LB per Cluster | N/A | N/A | 2 |

always-quoted-n-plus-one.statement: Private Service Edge 3 and Private Service Edge 5 are always quoted with N+1 redundancy to meet the Zscaler SLA requirements; the second node also covers traffic bursts and hardware failure.

quotes: Private Service Edge 3 is always quoted with N+1 redundancy to meet the Zscaler SLA requirements and ensure service continuity.
Private Service Edge 5 is always quoted with N+1 redundancy to meet the Zscaler SLA requirements and ensure service continuity.

over-5gbps-needs-dedicated-and-review.statement: Any deployment requiring more than 5 Gbps of total throughput must include the Dedicated LB hardware and must be reviewed by Zscaler Cloud Operations.

quotes: Any deployment requiring more than 5 Gbps of total throughput must include the Dedicated LB hardware.
Any deployment requiring more than 5 Gbps of total throughput must be reviewed by Zscaler Cloud Operations.

pse5-above-1gbps.statement: For more than 1 Gbps of download throughput, the sizing section recommends deploying Private Service Edge 5.

quotes: For more than 1 Gbps of download throughput, Zscaler recommends deploying Private Service Edge 5.

worked-examples.statement: Worked examples on the page: 800 Mbps download plus 240 Mbps upload is 1.04 Gbps total on a 1GE port, served by two Private Service Edge 3 nodes; 1.8 Gbps download plus 540 Mbps upload is 2.34 Gbps total on a 10GE port, served by two Private Service Edge 5 nodes; 1.75 Gbps download needs 2 x Private Service Edge 5, and 2.45 Gbps and 3.5 Gbps download each need 3 x Private Service Edge 5.

quotes: The total throughput that the Private Service Edge cluster must support is 1.04 Gbps (800 Mbps + 240 Mbps = 1.04 Gbps).
The total throughput that the Private Service Edge cluster must support is 2.34 Gbps (1.8 Gbps + 540 Mbps = 2.34 Gbps).
| 1.75 Gbps | 525 Mbps | 2.27 Gbps | 2 x Private Service Edge 5 |
| 3.5 Gbps | 1.05 Gbps | 4.55 Gbps | 3 x Private Service Edge 5 |

above-5gbps-dedicated-budget.statement: A deployment above 5 Gbps of total throughput must use the Dedicated LB design (Private Service Edge 5 with Dedicated LB), so its per-node address and port budget is the Dedicated LB budget (6 service addresses, an MTS address, up to 8 x 10GE ports), not the integrated LB budget.
above-5gbps-dedicated-budget.conditions: Compares the two budgets as the ip-requirements page states them; Zscaler Cloud Operations' review may change the design.

pse3-above-1gbps-tension.title: PSE 3 versus PSE 5 above 1 Gbps of download
pse3-above-1gbps-tension.detail: The page says a Private Service Edge 3 cluster handles up to 1.2 Gbps of download, yet recommends Private Service Edge 5 for more than 1 Gbps of download, and the design table sizes Private Service Edge 3 for 1 Gbps. The page does not say whether 1.0 to 1.2 Gbps is a supported PSE 3 range or headroom. Unverified legacy statement (corrected here): the legacy table labelled '~24 Gbps' as 'Max total' for the Dedicated LB design; the source labels it maximum upload throughput per cluster.
